INSTRUCTIONS TO THE SCHOOL
1. Each school offering Computer Science as a subject should produce two copies of the
 instructions. One copy of the instructions for the headteacher and the other copy for the
 teacher of Computer Science.
2. The headteacher and the teacher of Computer Science should each read the instructions
 carefully. Relevant information should then be conveyed to the learners as soon as possible
 to enable them carry out the project in good time.
3. There is only one project. It is necessary for the teacher of Computer Science to discuss
 the requirements of the project with the learners and the headteacher so as to understand
 what is required.
 This advance instruction has 12 printed page.
 Turn Over

INSTRUCTIONS TO THE HEADTEACHER
1. The school presenting learners for School Based Assessment on Computer Science is required
 to provide each group of learners with the following:
 (a) Regular learners
 (i) A disassembled desktop computer system comprising of various peripheral devices.
 (ii) Sufficient work areas to enable the learners carry out the project comfortably.
 (iii) Materials for labelling the physical parts of a computer. The materials can be made from
 locally available resources.
 (b) Learners with physical impairment
 (i) A disassembled desktop computer system comprising of various peripheral devices.
 (ii) Sufficient work areas to enable the learners carry out the project comfortably.
 (iii) Materials for labelling the physical parts of a computer. The materials can be made from
 locally available resources and technological interventions.
 (iv) Assistive devices where applicable such as:
 • Universal communication board, text to speech software or lip-readers for learners with
 speech difficulties
 • Universal cuffs, wrist/arm braces and arm holders for learners with manipulation
 difficulties. The learners can also use alternative functional body parts.
 • Adjustable work areas to accommodate learners with varied heights.
 (c) Learners with visual impairment
 (i) A disassembled desktop computer system comprising of various peripheral devices.
 (ii) Sufficient work areas to enable the learners carry out the project comfortably.
 (iii) Materials for labelling the physical parts of a computer. The materials can be made from
 locally available resources.
 (iv) Instructions in large print for those with low visual challenges.
 (v) Assistive devices and technological interventions where applicable such as:
 • Magnifying lenses, screen readers and magnifiers for learners with low vision.
 • Braille keyboards for blind learners.
 (d) Learners with hearing impairment
 (i) A disassembled desktop computer system comprising of various peripheral devices.
 (ii) Sufficient work areas to enable the learners carry out the project comfortably.
 (iii) Materials for labelling the physical parts of a computer. The materials can be made from
 locally available resources.
 (iv) Assistive devices such as hearing aids to be allowed for the Hard of Hearing.
2. Facilitate learners with any form of video recording devices.
3. Provide means of electronic storage to the teacher of Computer Science to store learners’
 activities.
4. The project should be carried out by learners in one week in the month of July 2023.
5. The scoring guide for the project will be uploaded on the KNEC portal together with other
 relevant
 documents. Each school should download all the relevant documents from the portal. The
 supervisor should make enough copies of the scoring guide and the learner’s declaration form for
 all the learners. The supervisor should accurately assess the learners’ projects using the scoring

6. The total score of each group of learners at the end of the project shall be transferred from the
 scoring guide to individual learner’s assessment sheet. The overall score for each learner will be
 transferred to the manual marksheet. The list in the manual marksheet shall be entered in an
 ascending order of assessment numbers.
7. It is the responsibility of the headteacher to ensure that the learners projects are marked, and the
 scores uploaded in the KNEC CBA portal at the stipulated time.

(f) For a learner with special needs, provide appropriate assistive devices and technological
